set.evidence_citation: USU News (Uniformed Services University), 'Dr. Norman Rich named Icon in Surgery,' 2 Nov 2017 (institutional record of 2nd MASH chief-of-surgery role)
set.notes: Rich served as Chief of Surgery, 2nd Surgical Hospital (Mobile Army), 1st Cavalry Division — Fort Bragg 1965, then An Khe, Republic of Vietnam — before returning to Walter Reed General Hospital in 1966 as its first vascular surgery fellow. Unit-level command mapped to the MASH System node (same granularity as the Kirk→MASH governance edge). [V16-B1 2026-07-18: retargeted from observational_study MASH→Rich (post-1950 scope violation; institution-sourced training-class edge). Appointment fact per USU institutional archive. PMIDs 5762414 and 15815826 citation-mcp-verified bibliographically (confidence 1.0) but not content-matched for the command title, so not used as evidence_type per content-match rule.]

Rich established the registry to meticulously track combat vascular injuries, driving the definitive transition from arterial ligation to immediate primary repair in modern vascular trauma. [Phase2 upgraded institutional_archive -> PMID: 5762414 on 2026-03-18] [Verified 2026-03-18 | Surgery 1969 | content_match] Rich NM, Hughes CW. 'Vietnam vascular registry: a preliminary report.' Surgery. 1969 Jan;65(1):218-226. The original registry publication by Rich himself. Follow-up PMID 1188624 (Surgery 1975) confirms registry established 1966 at Walter Reed Army Medical Center. [Norman Rich died 2026-06-18 (USU News obituary); 'Present' end-of-range semantics to be revisited at next temporal audit.]
